conditions: Finite states, unrestricted asset holdings and a traded strictly positive payoff; the original prices admit strictly positive state prices.
relations.use: Calculate claim price bounds and verify the original pricing and sub/superhedge equations through the existing econ-data owner.

conditions: An observed adjustment set contains no descendant of treatment and blocks every back-door path; the target treatment has positive support within its strata.
relations.use: Standardize conditional outcomes over the target population covariate distribution.

conditions: The observed mediator intercepts every directed treatment-outcome path, has no open back-door path from treatment, and its back-door paths to outcome are blocked by treatment; every conditional distribution in the formula has observed support.
relations.use: Combine the treatment-induced mediator distribution with treatment-standardized mediator outcome means.

conditions: Binary treatment, conditional exchangeability and overlap identify the adopted population ATE or treated-population ATT.
relations.use: Select DoubleMLIRM with score ATE or ATTE and match the nuisance regressions to that target.

conditions: A partially linear conditional mean and positive residual treatment variation define the common slope; under heterogeneous binary treatment effects the residualized coefficient uses conditional-variance weights.
relations.use: Select DoubleMLPLR and match partialling-out or IV-type nuisance regressions to its score.

conditions: The outcome is nonnegative, its conditional mean is exponential in the adopted regressors and effects, and identification and a finite solution hold; covariance follows the sampling and assignment units.
relations.use: Use Poisson quasi-likelihood for the adopted mean. Match effects, exposure and covariance to fepois or the documented existing poisson execution path.

conditions: Project outcomes, exogenous and endogenous regressors, and excluded instruments on the same fixed-effect space; the residualized instruments satisfy exclusion and the rank condition.
relations.use: Use the fixed-effect IV formula in feols and retain structural residuals, fitted observations, covariance and small-sample settings.
Use the Bellman contraction and fixed-point residual bound to separate iteration error from the approximation of the original operator.

conditions: Discount weights are 1, beta*delta, beta*delta^2, ...; the adopted future-self prediction and commitment set determine realized choices.
relations.use: Use the separate current-self maximization and delta-discounted policy value. For sophisticated finite-horizon choice, solve both recursions backward.

conditions: The adopted growth or saving model has differentiable primitives and an interior Euler root; monotonicity, strict concavity and endpoint signs determine the unique root. Boundary choices use the original Euler inequality.
relations.use: Compare Bellman maximization, fixed-policy evaluation and Euler root updates on the same model, grid, integration draws and boundary treatment.

conditions: State transitions are linear, costs are quadratic, actions range over real vectors, each best-response Hessian is positive definite, and the joint policy coefficient matrix is nonsingular. The adopted stationary solution has finite discounted values and satisfies both Riccati equations and the discounted terminal condition.
relations.use: Pass original transition matrices and beta to the documented Python or Julia nnash interface; evaluate policies, values, closed-loop transitions and unilateral deviations.

conditions: The finite two-player zero-sum game has perfect recall, legal information-set strategies and terminal payoffs. Counterfactual regret uses opponent and chance reach; the average strategy uses own reach.
relations.use: Evaluate the average policy by both best responses; NashConv is their gain sum and exploitability is half that sum.

conditions: Households observe the aggregate state and distribution; aggregate and employment transitions, borrowing constraints, competitive prices and the selected aggregate-state approximation are specified.
relations.use: Solve household policies for a forecast rule, simulate distributions, regress end-of-period aggregate assets on current aggregate resources by state, and update the coefficients with the documented damping convention.

conditions: The target integrand has a finite absolute first moment and the proposal is positive wherever f*p is nonzero. The iid variance and standard error additionally require the integral of f^2*p^2/q to be finite.
relations.use: Select the proposal from the target weighted integrand and its second moment; compare the named variance and standard error for the same integral.

conditions: Consumption policies are represented on a grid and continuation marginal utility is interpolated and integrated.
relations.use: Use the grid, interpolation, quadrature and original-equation comparison in DYN-04.

conditions: The coupled Riccati calculation solves the joint policy coefficient system and each positive-definite best-response system.
relations.use: Check the rank of the joint policy coefficient matrix and the positive definiteness of the individual best-response systems. Map their dimensions to the documented nnash input and evaluate the original residuals.
